pois.name: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur
pois.description: Romano-Byzantine basilica at the summit of Montmartre (83m). Its gleaming white travertine self-cleans in the rain. Highest viewpoint in Paris.

pois.name: Moulin Rouge
pois.description: The world's most famous cabaret, opening in 1889. The red windmill on Boulevard de Clichy. Toulouse-Lautrec painted its dancers here.

pois.name: Place du Tertre
pois.description: The village square that predates Paris's absorption of Montmartre. Artists set up easels here year-round — a living street art gallery.

pois.name: Musée de Montmartre
pois.description: The oldest building on the Butte, where Renoir, Utrillo and Suzanne Valadon had studios. Gardens overlook the Montmartre vineyard.

pois.name: Vignes de Montmartre
pois.description: Paris's only remaining vineyard, planted 1933. Produces ~800 bottles per year of Pinot Noir. Harvested every October in a village festival.
